newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta's Bank of Valletta makes record profit.
newsitem.headline: Malta's Bank of Valletta makes record profit.

text.p: Bank of Valletta, Malta's second largest bank, announced a record pre-tax profit of Lm13.7 million ($38 million) for the year ending September 30, up 29.6 percent from the Lm10.5 million ($29.19 million) profit made last year.
The bank said the financial year witnessed sustained balance sheet growth with group total assets increasing to Lm914.5 million ($2.54 billion) from Lm800.2 million ($2.2 billion) last year.
Bank chairman John Grech said the excellent performance had led the board of directors to propose a gross dividend of 7c per share up from 5.4c last year.

"The excellent results together with the bank's success in consolidating its position as a major player in Malta's financial services sector, attest positively to the validity of the strategy of relationship banking which the group is implementing," he said.

Deposits by customers increased from Lm 640 million ($1.7 billion) to Lm719.9 million ($2.0 billion) while net advances to customers increased from Lm376.1 million ($1.04 billion) to Lm 449.1 million ($1.24 billion).
Total shareholders' funds rose to Lm52.5 million ($145.9 million) against Lm45 million ($125.1 million) the previous year.
Group net asset value per share as of September 30 stood at Lm1.14 compared to Lm0.97 for the year before.
Bank of Valletta was privatised two years ago but the government has a 25 percent stake and appoints the chairman.
